sentences.text: The accused Nos.2 and 3 in C.C.No.198 of 1991 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Chengannur, have filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 2 (ia) (a) and 7(i) r/w Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Chengannur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.

The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 17.9.1991 at about 10 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 6 packets of coriander powder, each packet having a weight of 100 grams each from the shop of the first accused.
The second and the third accused persons were the manufacturers of the food item.
After sampling as per law, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.
The Public Analyst filed Ext. P12 report stating that the sample contained 7% of wheat starch and was therefore adulterated.
After complying with the legal formalities, the complaint was filed before the court.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts. P1 to P22 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 and DW2 were examined and Exts.D1 to D4 were marked for the revision petitioners.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P12 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act .

Therefore, Ext. P12 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case as adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Jose Joseph vs State Of Kerala on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179837007/
2

entities.text: Jose Joseph vs State Of Kerala on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pepsico India Holdings (supra).
A Division Bench of this Court in judgment dated 17-11-2015 in Crl.M.C. No. 417 of 2011 held that the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) is applicable to all cases.
In the said circumstances, the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below cannot be sustained.

In the result, this revision petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 2 (ia) (a) and 7(i) r/w Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the revision petitioners are acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bond of the revision petitioners stand cancelled and they are set at liberty.
B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR JUDGE Scl/11.01.2016
